about: Facts for the public 'Become a substitute' page. Every entry names its source and the date it was last checked (verified_on). Re-check entries older than 120 days; the settings screen lists them.

steps: Check whether you need fingerprints: only if you lived, worked or studied outside Wisconsin (another state, a US territory, Canada or Great Britain) in the last 20 years since age 17. If so, book Fieldprint (fieldprintwisconsin.com, code FPWIDPITeach) and pay about $40.

Scan your documents as PDF, Word, JPG or text, 2 MB or smaller each: an official transcript and your substitute-training certificate (or form PI-1633 if a district trained you; form PI-1975 if you're on the educator-program path).

Sign in to ELO (Educator Licensing Online), answer the setup questions, then choose 1-Teacher Category → S-Teacher – Short Term Substitute License [T910] → Request Short-term Substitute License [1910], attach your documents and submit.

Wait for DPI's confirmation email, then choose “Submit C&C and Payment”: answer the 14 Conduct & Competency questions and pay $135 by Mastercard, Visa or Discover credit card (no debit cards, no refunds).

Track the application on DPI's status page. Typical processing is 6–8 weeks, 8–12 if you've lived out of state. Meanwhile, keep going with employer applications: they don't wait on the permit, only your first day of work does.
tips: ELO is offline every Wednesday 10 pm to Thursday 2 am.
DPI runs its own background check on every application; an employer's check doesn't replace it.
Your permit lasts 3 years. Renew it in ELO with a new application before it expires.
dpi.employer_onboarding_note: Estimate: EDUStaff applicants report about 2 weeks from application to activation.

permit_a.name: Three-Year Short-Term Substitute Teacher Permit — degree path
permit_a.who: Associate degree or higher, plus a DPI-approved substitute teacher training course (a bachelor's degree doesn't exempt you from the training).
permit_a.allows: Any subject and grade, up to 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Valid 3 years.

permit_b.name: Three-Year Short-Term Substitute Teacher Permit — educator-program path
permit_b.who: Age 20 or older, enrolled in a Wisconsin approved educator preparation program (junior standing if it leads to a bachelor's), with 15 hours of classroom observation. Your program confirms this on form PI-1975. No separate training course is required.
permit_b.allows: Any subject and grade, up to 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Valid 3 years.

long_term.name: Five-Year Long-Term Substitute License
long_term.who: Completed an approved educator preparation program and hold, or are eligible for, a Wisconsin (or equivalent) teaching license. Retired teachers whose license expired can use this route.
long_term.allows: Long-term assignments in your license area, plus short-term (45 days or less) outside it. Valid 5 years.

none.name: Not eligible for a substitute teacher permit yet
none.who: DPI's permits need at least an associate degree, or enrollment in an educator preparation program.
none.allows: Options: finish an associate degree (Wisconsin technical colleges offer Foundations of Teacher Education), or start as a paraprofessional or support-staff substitute, which many districts and EDUStaff also hire for.

long_term_note: A permit caps you at 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Longer assignments need the Five-Year Long-Term Substitute License in that subject, or a One-Year License with Stipulations that the district requests ($140, and you must enroll in an educator program). Special-education assignments over 45 days need a special-education license.

training.next: Scheduled after you apply to EDUStaff
Start any time; pass the assessment with 85%

training.tied: The district confirms it on form PI-1633

delays.title: DPI takes 6–8 weeks to issue a permit
delays.cost: Six to eight weeks before your first paid day; eight to twelve if you need fingerprints.
delays.around: Apply to employers the same week you apply to DPI. Their applications, interviews and onboarding don't need the permit; only your first day does. The timeline above shows the difference.

delays.title: Every employer onboards you from scratch
delays.cost: Each district or agency runs its own application, references, background check, TB test, orientation and I-9: a few hours to two weeks each.
delays.around: One EDUStaff or Kelly Education application covers every district that agency serves, so pick an agency that serves several of the districts you want (step 3 shows which). Gather your transcript, training certificate and reference letters once and reuse them everywhere.
delays.nofix: Districts that hire their own subs each need their own application.

delays.title: Daily sub jobs aren't posted anywhere public
delays.cost: You can't see the actual day-to-day work until you're onboarded, so it's hard to tell which employer will keep you busy.
delays.around: Treat substitute postings as pool openings and join the pools that cover your area. Once you're active, keep your availability current in Frontline or Red Rover so jobs are offered to you.

delays.title: The same training costs anywhere from $0 to $80
delays.cost: Up to $80 for a certificate that's free elsewhere.
delays.around: If you're applying to EDUStaff anyway, its free Guest Teacher Workshop counts. Some districts train their own subs for free and confirm it on form PI-1633.

delays.title: DPI's $135 fee is credit-card only and non-refundable
delays.cost: Apply for the wrong license and the $135 is gone. Debit cards are refused, and ELO is offline every Wednesday 10 pm to Thursday 2 am.
delays.around: Confirm which license fits (step 1) before you pay, and use a Mastercard, Visa or Discover credit card.

delays.title: Some employers ask for more than DPI does
delays.cost: An associate degree meets DPI's rule, but Milwaukee Public Schools requires a bachelor's degree for subs.
delays.around: Step 3 shows each employer's degree rule. With an associate degree, focus on employers that follow DPI's rule (EDUStaff and Kelly Education do).

delays.title: A permit stops at 45 days in one classroom
delays.cost: Long-term assignments, often the best paid, end at day 45 for permit holders. Special-education ones longer than that need a special-education license.
delays.around: If you hold a bachelor's degree and want long-term work, ask the district about a One-Year License with Stipulations ($140, and you enroll in an educator program).

delays.title: Each district sets its own pay, and who employs you decides your retirement plan
delays.cost: Posted day rates here run from {pay_min} to {pay_max}. Agency subs get a 401(k) instead of WRS, Wisconsin's public pension.
delays.around: Compare posted pay for each route in step 3. If WRS matters to you, apply directly to districts that hire their own subs: you join WRS if you're expected to work 880 or more hours a year.
delays.nofix: No one outside the district can change its pay rate.

checklist.about: Phases run on the reader's own timeline: training, then DPI, with employer steps during the DPI wait. 'if' limits a task to readers it applies to: training, prints, permit. 'how' names a how-to block in the template.

tasks.text: Order an official transcript, as an electronic PDF if your college offers one. DPI and most employers ask for it.
Ask three people to be your references. MPS wants three letters under 3 years old; EDUStaff asks for at least one. Ask once and reuse the letters.
Sign up for a DPI-approved substitute training course.
Book fingerprints with Fieldprint (code FPWIDPITeach, about $40).
Pick where you want to sub (step 3) so you know which applications to file.
Finish the training course and save the completion certificate.
Apply to the employers you picked now. They don't wait on your permit; only your first day does.
Apply in ELO and pay the $135 fee by credit card.
Finish each employer's onboarding: online modules, workshop or orientation, interview, background check.
Get a TB test if an employer asks, and keep the receipt (some reimburse it).
Bring I-9 identity documents to onboarding in person. Don't email or upload them.
Check your application on DPI's status page every week or two.
Tell each employer your permit is issued; they confirm it on DPI's license lookup.
Set up Frontline or Red Rover and enter your availability, so daily jobs are offered to you.
Put your license's expiry date in your calendar (a permit lasts 3 years, the long-term license 5) and renew in ELO before it lapses.
On a permit, keep any one assignment to 45 consecutive days or less.
